did.unittitle: Kanoo family papers regarding Ford automobile dealerships
did.abstract: Correspondence between Khalil bin Ebrahim Kanoo, of Bahrain, his son, Ebrahim bin Khalil Kanoo, and the Ford Motor Company's Middle East branch headquarters in Alexandria, Egypt, concerning imports and sales of Ford automobiles in the Gulf region, in particular with reference to the Kanoo family's dealership in Dubai, 1950-1951.

accessrestrict.head: Conditions governing access
accessrestrict.p: The Kanoo family papers are open and available for use in the Archives and Special Collections department of the New York University Abu Dhabi Library.

acqinfo.head: Immediate source of acquisition
acqinfo.p: The collection was acquired by purchase, November 2022.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: The Kanoo family papers are arranged in three series, and then chronologically within each series.

bioghist.head: Biographical note
bioghist.p: Khalil bin Ebrahim Kanoo was a member of the family that established the namesake Bahrain-based trading company, founded by Yusuf bin Ahmed Kanoo (1868-1945)in 1890. The relationship between Yusuf and Khalil Kanoo is unclear, although some sources indicate that they may have been cousins. Khalil, who often went by the name "Khalil Ebrahim Kanoo," founded an automotive trading company in Bahrain in 1928, and appears to have been the director of that company until the late 1960s, at which point it was rebranded as the International Motor Trading Agency, W.L.L. (IMTA) in 1969, and was appointed to be the sole distributor for Mazda motor cars in Bahrain, a position that its successor company holds to this day.

In January 2025, IMTA was rebranded as Khalil Kanoo Motors, W.L.L. The company has expanded its automotive portfolio to include--in addition to Mazda--other global brands such as JAC Motors, BAIC, Arcfox EV, Goodyear Tyres, Sailun Tyres, Veedol Lubricants, ENEOS Oil, and Strong Batteries.

Ebrahim bin Khalil Kanoo, a son of Khalil Ebrahim, was born in 1920, and followed his father's footsteps in the automotive trade. As seen in the present collection of papers, he was active in his father's business as early as the late 1940s and early 1950s, when he had been appointed to briefly manage the company's Ford dealership in Dubai. Subsequently he held a variety of other positions in his family's businesses, although there are no indications as to whether the Kanoo's Ford dealership in Dubai continued past the early 1950s (the present-day concession for selling Ford vehicles in Dubai and Abu Dhabi is held by Al Tayer Motors). In 1967, he started a separate company to import the first Toyotas to Bahrain, and the company that he founded, Ebrahim K. Kanoo, continues to be the primary dealer for Toyota and Lexus vehicles in Bahrain. Today, his sons, Mohamed and Fuad, continue to serve as chairman and vice-chairman of that company.

scopecontent.head: Content Description
scopecontent.p: The Kanoo family automotive collection consists of correspondence between Khalil bin Ebrahim Kanoo, of Bahrain, his son, Ebrahim bin Khalil Kanoo, and the Ford Motor Company's Middle East branch headquarters in Alexandria, Egypt, concerning imports and sales of Ford automobiles in the Gulf region, in particular with reference to the Kanoo family's dealership in Dubai, 1950-1951.

At the time of acquisition, the correspondence was initially housed in the remains of two contemporary file folders, one labeled "File 52A. Sales Letters, 1950" and the other "File No. 62, Dubai correspondence, 1951." The contents of the latter file largely consisted of correspondence between Khalil Ebrahim Kanoo, based at the company's headquarters in Bahrain, with various representatives of Ford Motor Company (Egypt) in Alexandria, as well as with a smaller subset of correspondence with Ebrahim Khalil, the son of Khalil Ebrahim, who was responsible for the management of the Kanoo family's Ford dealership in Dubai. Most of the letters were numbered on the upper right hand margin of the page, showing the order in which they were initially filed. Since the correspondence from January - April 1950 seemed to pertain to the more general operations of the Kanoo family's automotive business in Bahrain and the Gulf region, those have been grouped separately from those dealing specifically with the operation of the Dubai branch, which are dated from September 1950 to March 1951.

A review of the correspondence shows some of the logistical difficulties of supplying vehicles, and vehicle parts, such as batteries, engine blocks, and tires, from factories based in Dagenham, England or Jersey City, U.S.A., with orders often delayed, and questions raised as to whether shipments should be sent to Dubai via Bahrain or Bombay. Responding to complaints of Ford's regional representatives in Egypt, and their concerns that the branch in Dubai was insufficiently staffed and that little thought had been given to a sales strategy for the Trucial States and Oman, Khalil Ebrahim responded in a letter of 4 February 1951 that business in Dubai had been "very dull" and that Dubai "is like a small village [and] the population of that end is very low, collectively [the] majority of the persons are very poor and there are no such nice places where the public should go…" Given that, Khalil's son Ebrahim, who had spent 8 months in Dubai, relocated back to Bahrain and left the business in Dubai in the hands of a manager.

The other original file of documents, the "Sales Letters," consisted of mimeographed letters addressed "To All Dealers Outside Egypt," and were meant to inform dealers throughout the Middle East of new products and promotions that customers in the region were to be made aware of. These letters, which were usually numbered and dated, are often referred to in the Kanoo correspodence, with Khalil Ebrahim sending numerous notes to the represenatives in Alexandria to confirm receipt of them, indicating the importance that Ford's representatives in Egypt placed on these sales letters as means of ensuring that the company's policies would be followed by their dealers in the region.
